m-jacksonville|2024-01-03|6fd02c96|20418.title: Chairman Howland said the City Council Strategic Planning Process will proceed with the adoption of a proposed list of Council priorities for FY24-25 at the February 6th Finance Committee meeting for introduction as a resolution for consideration by the full Council at the next council meeting. Council members will receive a memo outlining the priority suggestion process and are invited to submit items for consideration. CM Carrico asked if the proposals should be district-specific or city-wide priorities; Mr. Howland said both are acceptable. He said that the amount of funding available is $8.8M, with $5M being allocated to a CIP reserve fund for downtown capital projects and $3.8M available for allocation by the council ($200,000 per council member). Proposals should be submitted on the request form provided to Mary Staffopoulos in the Office of General Counsel and to Council Auditor Kim Taylor by noon on January 25th. Council members can have noticed meetings before that date to talk about potential shared projects and priorities.

m-jacksonville|2024-01-03|6fd02c96|5faef.title: Phillip Peterson explained the request for the emergency. CM Carrico asked about the proposed uses of the funds. Joe Johnson, ECA for the bill’s sponsor - CM Amaro - said that it will be used for items like palm tree trimming (not supported by the Public Works Department) and blight remediation, and could still be used for traffic calming if a specific need arises. Kim Taylor said that Public Works’ funding for trees is prioritized for safety purposes, not aesthetics, so this allocation would fund that sort of work. In response to a question from CM Arias, Public Works Director Nina Sickler said there is approximately $11M appropriated in the current budget specifically for extra mowing cycles and litter pickup which is now under contract for those specific uses. Mr. Arias recommended that changes be made to Public Works’ policies to make this type of expenditure for aesthetic purposes possible. CM Gaffney, Jr. asked for clarification about the source of the funds and the intended uses. CM Lahnen said there is a need for more palm tree trimming that is frequently requested by constituents. Ms. Sickler said there is not currently a policy regarding tree trimming for aesthetic purposes. She cautioned against spending available tree funds for aesthetic trimming early in the fiscal year before the tropical storm season hits later in the summer when there may be a great need for that funding to deal with storm aftermath.
